Dear Dr. Gallagher,

Thank you for seeing Ms. Elena Vance, a 48-year-old administrative assistant, for a comprehensive evaluation. Her routine blood work, including a metabolic panel and complete blood count, was completely normal, and she does not smoke. She takes a daily multivitamin.

Ms. Vance presents with a remarkably tall, long-limbed frame, an excavated anterior chest wall, and a mild thoracolumbar spinal curvature. She has long, slender digits and flat feet, alongside marked generalized ligamentous laxity and a history of repeated shoulder and patellar dislocations. Dynamic cervical radiographs revealed hypermobility of the cervical spine, and her recent bone density scan demonstrated mild osteopenia without signs of joint degeneration. Her lower limbs show straight alignment without knock-knee deformity, and she has no history of clubfoot.

On craniofacial examination, she exhibits widely separated eyes, flattened cheekbones, a recessed small lower jaw, a steep vaulted palate, a split uvula, and slate-blue sclerae. Her skull shape is normocephalic rather than elongated, her forehead lacks frontal bossing, her nasal profile is unremarkable, and her ears are normally positioned. There are no epicanthal folds. Her visual acuity is 20/20 without nearsightedness, extraocular alignment is straight with no squint, and slit-lamp exam confirmed clear corneas with no conical distortion.

Her skin is distinctly hyperelastic and translucent, revealing prominent venous patterning, lower extremity varicosities, easy ecchymoses, and silvery stretch marks on her abdomen and thighs; prior surgical incisions have healed firmly without paper-thin scarring. Her history is notable for repairs of both a periumbilical and a groin hernia, as well as an established allergy to tree nuts. Recent cardiac imaging confirmed billowing mitral leaflets with a regurgitant jet, while ruling out a persistent arterial duct. Contrast angiography revealed marked looping and elongation across her arterial tree, and lumbar MRI documented lumbosacral dural ectasia.

I would appreciate your expert opinion regarding an overarching assessment and guidance on her ongoing surveillance.

Sincerely,

Dr. Marcus Reed, MD
